mentions.name: CertKit
mentions.description: CertKit is a TLS certificate automation service that uses Let's Encrypt by default and handles ACME challenge validation via delegated DNS: it runs the DNS and users just CNAME to it, so no DNS credentials need to be shared. It acts as a central clearinghouse for certificates so every machine in a high-availability web farm gets the same cert without hitting Let's Encrypt rate limits, and it supports painful Windows workloads such as IIS and Exchange. It left beta last month.
mentions.problem: Manual TLS certificate management across on-prem and HA workloads, including Let's Encrypt rate limits and the risk of sharing DNS credentials.
mentions.audience: People running on-prem workloads, including HA web farms and Windows workloads like IIS and Exchange.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm working on https://www.certkit.io.  It started as a solution to handle TLS certificate automation for my other SaaS products, but we realized other people who run on-prem workloads might get something out of it.
